items.text: Cam Skattebo is the sharpest riser at RB — now going RB18 after recovering from a serious leg and ankle injury, sharing the top of the Giants depth chart with Tyrone Tracy Jr. at RB44. That 26-spot gap is the market betting hard on one side of a committee that isn't settled (Yahoo, 8/18)

Bucky Irving at RB20 opened camp at full speed after offseason shoulder surgery and is positioned for the majority of Tampa's carries. In a league paying 0.1 per rush attempt, a lead back at RB20 with no health cloud is the profile this scoring overpays you for

Stefon Diggs signed a one-year deal with Washington on Aug 7 and is still being drafted at WR49 — the market hasn't repriced the role yet. Reporting expects that number to climb well before Week 1 (Yahoo, 8/18)

MarShawn Lloyd is the best late-round handcuff on the board at RB60 — Josh Jacobs' groin injury has pushed him into extensive first-team work in Green Bay. Zero cost, real upside if Jacobs misses regular-season time
Ricky Pearsall is ruled out for all of 2026 after PCL surgery and was still carrying draftable ADP as recently as two weeks ago. Do not draft him at any price

Jonathon Brooks continues climbing off consecutive ACL tears — the gap between Chuba Hubbard at RB32 and Brooks at RB36 has narrowed to almost nothing, which means Carolina's backfield is now a coin flip priced as if it isn't
Courtland Sutton is the notable faller — Jaylen Waddle's arrival in Denver ends several seasons as the unquestioned lead receiver and caps his target ceiling

Daniel Jones is getting a market bump on reports he's practicing without limitation post-Achilles. Relevant here only as a late QB dart — this league pays 4 per pass TD and 0.05 per pass yard, so QB is the last place to spend up

CONFIRMED — draft_order is populated and you are slot 11 of 12, not slot 3. Your picks: 11, 14, 35, 38, 59, 62, 83, 86, 107, 110, 131, 134, 155, 158, 179, 182. Every slot-3 recommendation from earlier this month is void

The 11/14 near-turn is a single decision, not two. Only two picks separate them and then nothing comes back for 20 selections. Take two complementary players — not two of the same archetype — because you are locking your roster shape until pick 35

Ten players are gone before you choose. Do not build a plan around a name who won't be there; identify which TIER survives to 11 and take the best of it. The upside of slot 11 is that you are never on the clock alone — you always pick twice in quick succession
The 14→35 gap is the danger zone. Twenty picks will strip one position bare; historically in 12-team PPR that is the second RB tier. If you want two startable backs, both need to come at 11/14

Wait on QB until the 83-110 range. Pass TDs are worth 4 and pass yards 0.05, compressing the position — spending pick 35 or 38 on an elite QB is a 50-pick premium at the one slot where you start exactly one player
Kicker at 182, your final pick, and not one round earlier. There is NO team-defense slot in this league — never draft one at any price

Because 12+ team defenses sit inside standard top-192 ADP and none will be drafted here, the board plays roughly 14 picks deeper than public ADP implies. Pick 182 is closer to ADP rank ~196 — late-round targets last longer than their numbers suggest

NO KEEPERS — the league setting says max_keepers: 1 but the league does not use it. That is good news for planning: nobody is removed from the pool, so public ADP maps cleanly onto this draft. In keeper leagues the top of the board is thinned unpredictably; here, the consensus board is the real board
